advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Scope `bare`/pinned-name resolution per-function (or track binding site) so a same-named pinned repo in a sibling fixture cannot mask an unpinned hand-built one.
evidence: tests/unit/test_bare_clone_source_upkeep_sweep.py:203-209: `bare = { name for name in (_bare_created_by(node) ...) if name is not None } - _pinned_names(tree)`
`_pinned_names` returns a flat set of names across the whole module (line 189-197), with no scoping to the function/fixture that built the bare repo
Reused fixture variable names like `remote`, `origin`, `bare` are common across a test module's multiple fixtures, so a collision is plausible and its miss is silent
advisory.finding: The sweep computes `bare` and subtracts `_pinned_names(tree)` as MODULE-WIDE name sets. If a module hand-builds a bare repo bound to a variable name (e.g. `remote`) in one fixture AND, in a different fixture, routes another repo through `init_bare_remote(remote)` under the SAME variable name, the module-wide pinned-names subtraction removes `remote` from `bare`, so the genuinely unpinned hand-built clone source becomes invisible. The guard then passes even though a violating clone remains.
scenarios: A future module that pins one remote and hand-builds another, both bound to `remote`
Refactors that consolidate variable naming across fixtures

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend `_clone_helpers`/helper-call resolution to cover posonly/kwonly params and keyword-passed source arguments (or assert the source is positional).
evidence: tests/unit/test_bare_clone_source_upkeep_sweep.py:181: `parameters = [argument.arg for argument in node.args.args]` — ignores `node.args.posonlyargs` and `node.args.kwonlyargs`

tests/unit/test_bare_clone_source_upkeep_sweep.py:223-225: `if position is None or position >= len(node.args): continue` then `_addressed(node.args[position])` — only positional call args are inspected, keyword args (`_clone_tickets(source=origin, ...)`) are never resolved
advisory.finding: `_clone_helpers` only inspects `node.args.args` and matches by bare parameter-name identity, and `scan_module` resolves helper calls only through positional `node.args`. A helper invoked with the clone source passed as a KEYWORD argument, or a helper whose source parameter is positional-only/keyword-only, is not resolved — the wrapped clone is missed. The wrapper-following coverage the docstring promises is therefore incomplete and its miss is silent.
scenarios: A future fixture wraps the clone in a helper and calls it with `source=origin` as a keyword
A helper declares the source parameter as keyword-only

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a scanner test that a bare-repo name appearing as a `-b`/`--branch` VALUE is not reported as a clone source (exercises the _VALUED_CLONE_FLAGS skip).
evidence: _clone_source lines 161-166: `if flag is not None and flag.startswith("-"): index += 2 if flag in _VALUED_CLONE_FLAGS else 1`

Named violating input: a module containing `subprocess.run(["git","clone","-b",str(remote),str(work),str(dst)])` where `remote` is hand-built bare and `work` is the real source — no test covers whether `remote` (a -b value) is wrongly flagged.
The offender/f-url fixtures use `-b tickets` and `-q` but never place a bare-repository NAME as a valued-flag argument, so the skip logic is not exercised for its discriminating case.
advisory.finding: The scanner's valued-clone-flag skip (_VALUED_CLONE_FLAGS at test_bare_clone_source_upkeep_sweep.py:54; consumed at _clone_source lines 161-166) is newly added behavior with no test. No test asserts that a bare name appearing as the VALUE of a valued flag (e.g. `git clone -b <bare-name> <realsource>`) is NOT reported as the clone source. A regression that dropped the `index += 2` branch would produce a false positive undetected.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a scanner test for a `--bare` argv with no trailing path operand (no-operand branch of _bare_created_by).
evidence: _bare_created_by lines 148-151: `# No operand, so the bare repository is the directory the call runs in.` / `return _addressed(argv[0]) if argv else None`

Named violating input: a module of the shape `_git(remote, "init", "-q", "--bare")` (the exact pre-fix shape in tests/integration/test_reclaim_bridge_history.py:112 before this change) followed by a clone of `remote` — no test asserts whether the no-operand branch attributes and flags it.
All _OFFENDER/_WRAPPED_OFFENDER/f-url fixtures pass `str(remote)` after `--bare`, exercising only the operand branch (lines 145-149).
advisory.finding: The scanner's no-operand `--bare` branch (_bare_created_by lines 150-151: falls back to `_addressed(argv[0])` when `--bare` has no trailing path operand) is newly added and untested. Every scan-test fixture builds the bare repo with an explicit trailing operand (`str(remote)` after `--bare`), so the fallback that attributes the bare repo to argv[0] is never executed.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a scanner test that a remote pinned via `apply_upkeep_pins` is treated as pinned (no finding), covering the second entry of _PINNING_FACTORIES.
evidence: test_the_sweep_detects_a_reintroduced_unpinned_clone_source only substitutes `init_bare_remote(remote)` (line 272); apply_upkeep_pins never appears in any fixture.

Named violating input: a module `subprocess.run(["git","init","--bare",str(remote)]); apply_upkeep_pins(remote); subprocess.run(["git","clone",str(remote),str(dst)])` — no test asserts it is treated as pinned (no finding).
advisory.finding: `apply_upkeep_pins` is listed in _PINNING_FACTORIES (line 57) so a remote pinned via apply_upkeep_pins is treated as pinned by _pinned_names (lines 189-197), but no test exercises this second factory. Only init_bare_remote appears in the fixed-form assertion (test_the_sweep_detects...:272). A regression dropping apply_upkeep_pins from _PINNING_FACTORIES would cause false positives on modules that pin via apply_upkeep_pins, undetected.
